scope: Each candidate's retained full statement, references and status discussion were read; fresh online queries checked for matching later complete results and announcements. Sources listed include retained primary comparators and sources surfaced online. The search log records retrieved snippets/selected primary passages. This is not an exhaustive proof of continued openness or a full proof audit of the cited literature.

104.review_note: Liehr's 2026 compact-support classification assumes a one-dimensional lattice; product/separable results are also restricted. The nonproduct-window counterexample is not an indicator window. No theorem for arbitrary finite-measure sets and arbitrary countable time-frequency sets found.

106.review_note: The 28 September 2026 version of Levitin and Polterovich proves odd buckling indices in the plane and some even indices with adjacent equal buckling eigenvalues. The 14 October 2026 Buoso-Lotoreichik paper explicitly leaves the general even planar case open; its counterexamples concern intrinsic manifolds, not Euclidean domains. The older all-index proof was withdrawn after an identified Lemma 4.2 error. Fresh searches through 30 October 2026 found no matching complete resolution or announced solution of the stated all-dimensional Euclidean comparison.

138.review_note: Full-boundary rough planar uniqueness, local smooth uniqueness and fractional exterior-data results have different hypotheses. The earlier anisotropic planar local theorem uses both local DN and ND maps; it does not establish this one arbitrary-patch map for L-infinity conductivities.

162.review_note: Subsequential Euler-invariant limits are known. Dependence on a changed viscosity exponent and effective finite-dimensional observable dynamics do not settle sequence independence of the full velocity law with one fixed noise covariance and the fixed Laplacian.

182.review_note: The fixed-temperature continuum percolation sharpness theorem does not locate a unique Gibbs-state threshold on the symmetric diagonal z=beta=lambda. Large-activity coexistence and random-field lattice results leave the full diagonal uniqueness/nonuniqueness assertion unresolved.

185.review_note: The question is the stationary continuum scaling limit with its specified exceptional-state extension and natural filtration. Ordinary Markov, Liouville variants and Voronoi crossing/universality results do not establish this exact strong Markov assertion.

193.review_note: Known monotone/summable/regularly varying branch-length criteria and the 2026 discrete-aggregation results do not give a necessary and sufficient compactness criterion for every bounded deterministic sequence in the continuous uniform-length attachment model.

215.review_note: The low-density periodic quantum limit is known to low perturbative orders or conditional on lattice statistics, and with added damping. These are not the unconditional fixed-coupling h=r trace limit in the target.

240.review_note: The general entropy weak-class target removes bounded-flux or smooth-reference assumptions. The current renormalized theorem requires bounded fluxes; whole-space weak existence and additive-friction strong results do not give arbitrary-coefficient weak uniqueness including vacuum.

241.review_note: The September Bousquet–Lamy result enlarges a sufficient global regime but retains a gap; its stronger explicit condition restricts competitors. Isotropic p-energies, second-variation stability and boundary regularity do not determine the full two-parameter global-minimality region.

246.review_note: The magnetic torus target uses Bialy's full ambient vertical no-conjugate-points convention in dimension >=3. The 2025 magnetic-curvature theorem retains an integral equality/curvature condition, and later entropy theorems add no-focal-point hypotheses. Conformally flat and zero-field cases do not settle arbitrary metrics.

247.review_note: Global hyperbolic polyhedron rigidity is stronger than infinitesimal/local rigidity. Euclidean dihedral-rigidity theorems, spherical counterexamples and conditional implications from the volume conjecture do not settle the exact hyperbolic global assertion.

248.review_note: The global smooth Riemannian S2 inequality is distinct from singular Finsler counterexamples, punctured-sphere sharp bounds and local Zoll optimality. The 2026 geodesic-dynamics primary discussion retains Calabi's bound as a conjecture.

251.review_note: The current near-equal-mass theorem covers all subcritical energies only for mu near 1/2; the Hill theorem is a limiting model. They do not give disk-like global sections for every finite mass ratio.

264.review_note: Polyhedral, ball and waveguide results do not determine a general smooth PEC obstacle from one fixed-frequency/direction/polarization plane wave. The broad 2016 claim remains withdrawn; acoustic and elastic boundary conditions are different.

282.review_note: The 2026 generic-geometry theorem gives nondegenerate multistationarity under extra conditions and only a bounded gain from degenerate roots; it does not equate the complete finite equilibrium capacity with nondegenerate capacity for every fixed network.

283.review_note: The August 2026 BBM classification concerns one reproduction mechanism and invariance under its full semigroup. Locally finite-intensity results and the opposite branching-convolution order do not classify every invariant point process for every offspring law in the stated assumptions.

284.review_note: The latest 2026 one-dimensional SGD paper explicitly says its logarithmic counterexamples use gradients of size sqrt(T) and do not settle uniformly almost-surely bounded gradients. Its iid additive-noise positive theorem, deterministic results, smooth interpolation and different schedules do not cover arbitrary adapted bounded oracles with the specified constant step.

300.review_note: The current Lissy–Lourme result is one-dimensional. Vanlaere's singular-Grushin work concerns boundary singularities in 2D or interior singularities in higher dimension; no full answer for Morancey's transmitting 2D interior model found.

308.review_note: Checked current Panazzolo-related work and the 2026 unbounded-canard paper. Holomorphic saddle loops, discontinuous switching fields and smooth regularizations do not give a uniform bound or counterexample for globally continuous affine fields on a fixed rectangular grid.

328.review_note: The discrete M/M/1 transformation is Bernoulli and the Brownian map has a Bernoulli factor. Neither proves ergodicity or Bernoulli isomorphism of the entire two-sided continuous Brownian-with-positive-drift transformation.

351.review_note: One-component space-time criteria and symmetry-breaking/norm inflation do not answer the unconditional initial-component question. General blowup announcements do not assert arbitrarily small critical H1/2 size of one initial component in this working class; modified, forced or anisotropically dissipative equations have different hypotheses.

384.review_note: The August boundary-thermalization work studies macroscopic superdiffusive transport, not the exact nonequilibrium fourth-order stationary energy covariance in the proposed inverse-operator formula. Neither a profile hydrodynamic limit nor local equilibrium proves that nonlocal covariance assertion.

385.review_note: Real-analytic or piecewise-constant injectivity, higher-dimensional convex-foliation results and microlocal cancellation of singularities do not prove qualitative unweighted injectivity for every smooth nontrapping surface allowing conjugate points.

386.review_note: The source gives conditional boundary-Cauchy estimates under pseudoconvexity/foliation hypotheses and special-case sharpness. Interior volumetric observations and qualitative unique continuation do not identify the optimal boundary-observed conditional-Holder region solely from visibility.

387.review_note: Current transport-twistor biholomorphism rigidity, local blow-downs and constant-curvature/perturbative coordinate results do not imply compact holomorphic hulls for every compact subset of every Anosov-surface transport twistor interior.

395.review_note: The 2026 exterior biharmonic-cavity paper uses an unbounded plate and two measurement sets. In-plane elasticity, time-harmonic scattering and one-measurement outer-boundary/rigid-inclusion results do not settle one static bending experiment for a free interior cavity in a bounded plate.

396.review_note: The current periodic smooth-data De Gregorio problem is broader than symmetry/sign classes. Instability of excited states, lower-regularity periodic blowup and real-line self-similar profiles do not resolve arbitrary smooth data on the circle.

397.review_note: The exact left-Caputo Volterra characteristic function and its complete complex zero multiset are required. Variable-order mixed derivatives with norming data, self-adjoint two-sided fractional operators and classical spatial Sturm–Liouville inverse results do not prove this one-spectrum theorem.

398.review_note: The target is the actual range of the unmodified electric far-field operator's quarter power for a PEC obstacle. Modified-operator, penetrable, static and waveguide factorization results avoid the middle-operator obstruction and do not establish this exact criterion.

399.review_note: The August 2026 classification proves invariance generally and the quasi-invariance equivalence only for finitely many active directions. A prescribed transport-flow obstruction is not Euler's self-consistent Gaussian flow. The infinitely-many-directions quasi-invariance target remains beyond these theorems.

402.review_note: The all-gamma singular-weight isomorphism theorem is known on disks and selected constant-curvature models. Tensor results on the Euclidean disk and asymptotically hyperbolic surfaces do not provide a suitable alpha-boundary-defining weight for every simple compact manifold.

405.review_note: The October regular-Lagrangian-flow theorem requires special BD and extra time regularity. BV theory, Euler energy conservation and fractional-Sobolev counterexamples do not establish uniqueness for every prescribed divergence-free L1-time BD velocity with arbitrary Cantor part.

413.review_note: Current hyperbolic p-Laplacian results add damping, sources or higher-order regularization. Local classical existence and measure-valued limits do not give or refute a global ordinary constitutive-flux, energy-admissible weak solution for every smooth multidimensional datum.

416.review_note: Yudovich existence and smooth/Gevrey trajectories are known, but not their real analyticity for every bounded vorticity. Holder-vorticity, regular-vortex-patch and different phase-space analyticity theorems add hypotheses.

423.review_note: The arbitrary-smooth-potential compact-resolvent implication is broader than polynomial or derivative-growth hypotheses. Local maximal hypoellipticity and electromagnetic compactness criteria do not automatically prove Helffer–Nier's full implication.

424.review_note: The sharp constant-field sum inequality is known. Variable-field bounds at Riesz order >=3/2, or different constants, do not prove the stated sharp order-one Li–Yau inequality for arbitrary smooth magnetic fields.

425.review_note: The source still leaves general domains open. Polyhedral-domain and nested-domain paths do not simultaneously provide fixed volume, both functional monotonicities and full gamma-continuity for every bounded open domain.

428.review_note: The 2026 sharp mixed boundary-area/volume normalization is different from sigma1 times boundary area^(1/(n-1)). Fixed-volume product, convex-only, exterior and manifold-metric results do not determine this supremum over all smooth Euclidean domains.

440.review_note: The arbitrary-step, all-exponent horizontal-gradient assertion remains beyond step-two/Heisenberg and restricted-exponent Riemannian-approximation theorems. Current searches found no complete arbitrary-Carnot resolution.

481.review_note: The one-dimensional entropy-dissipation result uses displacement convexity absent in the plane. Higher-dimensional existence/discrete dissipation or different fractional fast-diffusion functionals do not establish this sharp whole-plane Riesz-energy inequality.

495.review_note: Checked Beliaev's Gaussian-field discussion and recent Cardy searches. Lattice/random-cluster Cardy results and Bargmann–Fock RSW bounds do not identify the exact Gaussian-field rectangle limit.

500.review_note: The official September announcement is restricted to formal dimension four. The general all-dimensional topological-manifold Singer statement remains beyond that theorem and the 2026 semismall-Albanese cases.

503.review_note: The unrestricted continuous-self-map plane-continuum problem is distinct from Cartwright–Littlewood theorems for maps extending to plane homeomorphisms. The 2025 primary article retains it; no complete newer announcement located.

504.review_note: Kuperberg's volume-preserving aperiodic construction is C1; unrestricted smooth counterexamples do not preserve volume. The smooth conservative S3 question remains separate from Reeb/contact and singular-contact variants.

505.review_note: The October Descartes recursion and topological-degree bounds do not yield a worst-case polynomial bound for the unsigned number of nondegenerate positive roots at fixed dimension. Random-coefficient expectations and the disproved product bound are different targets.

509.review_note: Complete noncompact full-holonomy examples and positive-Einstein constructions do not construct a closed simply connected Ricci-flat SO(n)-holonomy manifold or exclude all such manifolds.

511.review_note: The apparent full Markus proof remains withdrawn in the current official arXiv record (v3). Ray-holonomy, centralizing-holonomy and metric special cases do not settle arbitrary volume-preserving affine connections.

516.review_note: The continuous Brownian half-line Lévy transformation is the target. Density/topological recurrence and sufficient conditions for exactness do not prove its ergodicity; no newer complete announcement found.

518.review_note: The latest author version improves the extension loss at a larger test threshold; it retains the simultaneous 2^D and exp(poly(D)) question. No later matching result was located.

521.review_note: Current cylindrical-cone uniqueness and near-multiplicity-two-plane theorems retain tangent-model or structural assumptions. Almost-everywhere regularity/singular-dimension announcements do not establish uniqueness at every singular point for Euclidean stationary integral varifolds.

522.review_note: The 2026 SIAM paper still has logarithmic losses. The September critical-Besov theorem imposes a bounded outer coefficient budget and different norms/classes; it does not establish the unrestricted Lipschitz-ball uniform lower bound.

523.review_note: The September 2026 high-dimensional-vector article retains dimension dependence, albeit log log m, in adaptive bounds. It does not make the infinite-dimensional noncompact inclusion approximable, nor prove an adaptive error floor in the expected-budget RMS model.

527.review_note: Arbitrarily slow approximation is known in dimension two and above. The recent scalar survey explicitly asks the autonomous one-dimensional smooth bounded case; results with Lipschitz drift, time-irregular coefficients or a particular scheme do not settle it.

531.review_note: Positive-sectional-curvature classifications and torus-symmetric or twistor-curvature theorems do not classify arbitrary positive Einstein metrics on standard S4. No active unrestricted resolution located; the torus-symmetry preprint's withdrawal is retained.

532.review_note: The October 2026 Streets–Tian announcement assumes compact homogeneous quotient structure. Nilmanifold, solvmanifold and surface cases leave arbitrary compact complex manifolds of dimension >=3 outside their scope.

533.review_note: The 2026 projectively-normal theorem has extra embedding/singularity hypotheses. Singular counterexamples and Ulrich-sheaf counterexamples are not smooth ideal-sheaf regularity counterexamples to this precise arbitrary-embedding question.

535.review_note: New 23 October 2026 paper by Yu Feng proves mutual absolute continuity with SLE3 for every subsequential thermal spin-interface limit, using uniformly controlled densities. It does not identify a unique full-sequence limit in all admissible Jordan domains. Thermal FK-interface and weak-interaction critical-universality announcements have different targets.

537.review_note: New 23 October 2026 angle-cocycle paper proves the implication under immersed straightening, including convex-projective manifolds. It does not prove every aspherical topological manifold admits such a structure. Nonpositively curved four-dimensional and scalar-curvature comparisons are likewise restricted.

538.review_note: Compact closed-geodesic infinitude, hyperbolic finite-volume theorems and geodesic flowers under end conditions do not imply a smooth periodic geodesic on every complete noncompact finite-volume manifold of dimension >=3.

545.review_note: Known finite-blocking flatness results impose nonpositive curvature, no conjugate points or regularity/separation of blockers. Translation-surface classifications permit conical singularities and do not classify arbitrary smooth Riemannian metrics.

546.review_note: The September 2026 profile-curve paper still leaves Angenent-torus uniqueness open. Noncompact genus-one shrinkers and tangent-flow uniqueness do not produce a compact embedded counterexample or classify all compact genus-one shrinkers.

547.review_note: The 2026 surfaces-with-symmetry result retains group symmetry. Fixed-conformal-class, higher-codimension and other-topology statements do not prove the unrestricted genus-g Lawson lower bound with its equality classification.

551.review_note: Regularity/classification of planar Mumford–Shah minimizers is not equality with the calibration dual. The source's gapless-duality conjecture for this jump-energy functional remains beyond integral-functional and thermal-insulation calibration results.

554.review_note: Searches retain the small-mixed-smoothness lower-bound gap. Frolov upper bounds, two-dimensional optimality, quantum Besov integration and particular-rule estimates do not settle unrestricted deterministic cubature in dimensions >=3.

561.review_note: The October 2026 survey retains removal of the logarithmic overhead for p<2. Uniform-norm hyperbolic-cross discretization, weighted rules and L2 sparsification are not the two-sided equal-weight L1 statement under the stated Nikolskii bound.

566.review_note: Analytic unstable elliptic equilibria are constructed in higher degrees of freedom; two-degree examples cited here have weaker regularity. The September 2026 density theorem requires at least five degrees and does not provide this analytic two-degree example.

568.review_note: Ullrich's 2026 all-s-number result treats symmetric operator balls. Its nonsymmetric convex-set extension yields a linear factor for Hilbert targets and a larger factor in general; it does not supply the requested general Banach-target randomized-error estimate.

569.review_note: The original randomized continuous-versus-algebraic-linear information question remains distinct from its solved worst-case counterparts. The 2026 survey uses different budget/error/measurability conventions; no exact-model resolution found.

571.review_note: The planar, parallelotope and equilateral cases are known. Euclidean or specified lp-norm theorems do not prove the bound and rigidity for all finite-dimensional norms; no matching general announcement located.

572.review_note: The Annals theorem settles dimension three; contact, codimension-one and inducing-scheme results add hypotheses. New examples of exponentially mixing flows and discrete Anosov-map results do not prove exponential mixing for every smooth mixing Anosov flow in all dimensions.

575.review_note: The first-exit maximum of planar random-walk local time is distinct from the wired-domain cover-time/last-vertex law. Searches found no matching complete scalar-maximum fluctuation theorem.

579.review_note: The current Holder nonembedding results impose extra Euclidean regularity in the gap above 1/2. Holder maps constructed below 2/3 need not be injective; the purported 2016 solution remains withdrawn.

580.review_note: Density-threshold improvements are partial and do not reach the strict planar >1/2 criterion. Higher-dimensional examples attain equality at 1/2 and are not counterexamples to the strict planar formulation.

584.review_note: Heilman's cylinder classification assumes product minimality and retains an exceptional curvature case. These conditions and the near-zero/one-volume strip cases leave the arbitrary fixed-dimension cylinder/complement inequality unresolved.

586.review_note: The October 15/16-line theorem handles only small complex rank-three arrangements. Numerical/generalized variants and conic-line counterexamples do not give a real free/nonfree hyperplane pair with the same full intersection lattice.

587.review_note: Known Goh-rank/corank/generic cases and analytic variants do not settle arbitrary smooth minimizing Sard. The September and October endpoint-map counterexamples explicitly distinguish nonminimizing abnormal curves from this minimizing assertion.

589.review_note: The 2025 multi-marginal optimality theorem still assumes continuous cost. Borel two-marginal results and infinite-valued multi-marginal counterexamples do not decide the finite nonnegative Borel case with an integrable marginal-sum bound.

591.review_note: Kahler, complex-threefold and 2026 Vaisman Calabi–Yau cases add hypotheses. Fundamental-group restrictions and statements about more general affine tensors do not imply local homogeneity of every compact holomorphic Riemannian metric.

593.review_note: September 2026 result verifies Berge for genus <=5; the tunnel-number-one theorem is another restricted case. Lens-space realization and purely cosmetic surgery assertions do not classify all knots admitting an integer lens-space surgery.

595.review_note: The 2026 fourfold work covers currently known families, and the newer polarized Galois theorem adds a Galois condition. Neither settles all smooth Picard-one Fano manifolds and arbitrary degree>1 self-maps.

599.review_note: Fixed nonzero parameters and a free Brownian endpoint are essential. Intermediate-disorder limits and directed-landscape results conditional on KPZ convergence do not prove the GOE fluctuation conjecture for this Poisson polymer.

601.review_note: July 2026 memory/query lower bounds force larger polynomial exponents, not superpolynomial queries for every exponent. Feasibility-oracle lower bounds do not automatically transfer to the narrower global-minimizer first-order model; no matching complete answer found.

602.review_note: The 2026 nonsmooth quasi-Newton paper retains assumptions on matrix eigenvalues that are not established for all executions. Smooth-convex, isolated-nonsmooth-minimum, one-dimensional rate and modified/L-BFGS results do not prove the u^2+|v| all-Armijo–Wolfe-sequence conjecture.

603.review_note: New light-structure relaxation results and free-material global-value/laminate results do not prove absence of suboptimal strong-L2 local stress minima for this fixed multiplier, ordered-isotropic two-phase relaxed compliance functional.

605.review_note: The later circle-discretization theory fixes the iteration time before the grid limit. It does not prove generic convergence for every growing sequence log N << m << sqrt N; simulations are not such a theorem.

611.review_note: The October modular prime-geodesic improvement still has exponent above 1/2. Congruence-class, averaged, weighted and Bianchi-manifold estimates do not establish this fixed modular-group pointwise square-root error.

615.review_note: Question is alpha-mixing of a finite-state stationary process implying Bernoulli isomorphism, with no rate. Beta-mixing, ordinary mixing and observable CLTs are different conditions/conclusions; the 2026 ICM discussion retains the question.

616.review_note: The corrected January 2026 Jang–Ryu version does not retain its earlier subcritical convergence argument. Critical damping alpha=3, rates for objective values, and bounded/strong-minimum special cases do not prove arbitrary-Hilbert weak convergence for 1<alpha<3.

620.review_note: Minty criteria giving maximality from surjective sum, or contact sets with splitting potentials, do not prove the converse for every maximally c-monotone set. Lim's nonmaximal example does not refute this premise.

621.review_note: The original expansion-including algorithm and every nondegenerate starting triangle are required. Restricted Nelder–Mead, quantitative step-frequency conditions, common-value convergence and 2026 statistical parameter heuristics do not prove convergence to the quadratic minimizer.

622.review_note: The one-dimensional minimax result is sharp up to logarithms; the requested exact order includes those factors for noisy bounded convex losses. Higher-dimensional hidden-curvature bounds and pseudo-1D models do not remove the remaining logarithmic uncertainty.

627.review_note: The exactness-region degree formula divides by an unknown projection degree. Reported computations, local Voronoi results and generic quadratic-optimization algebraic degrees do not prove generic componentwise degree one for every 2<=m<=n.

630.review_note: Current CPE results impose dimension, curvature, contact or stability hypotheses. An Einstein classification assumes the desired conclusion and cannot prove it for every nonconstant CPE metric; withdrawn full claims are not accepted.

631.review_note: The target allows distinct arbitrary anisotropic positive quadratic forms on full gradients. Results for symmetric strains, compatible finite-well sets, or one quadratic form do not establish the stated universal envelope equality; no complete newer resolution located.

634.review_note: Retains real L2-local potentials with a small local form bound in every dimension. Later many-body Lebesgue-potential UCP and non-interacting Hohenberg–Kohn results do not establish this high-dimensional general form-bound conjecture.

637.review_note: The three-cell 2026 negative-correlation result covers only a subrange of correlations. It does not settle all q>=3 and -1<rho<0. Unequal-mass comparisons and conditional hyperstability classifications do not refute or prove the centered-simplex benchmark here.

639.review_note: The published noisy-information paper leaves the infinite-dimensional diagonal example open. Noise-free exponential accuracy and fixed-noise polynomial order do not give the joint n,delta asymptotic with uniform constants.

642.review_note: Known special driftless subordinators and decompositions into two clocks satisfying (H) do not imply (H) for every driftless infinite-activity subordinator; closure under arbitrary sums is not supplied.

644.review_note: An actual CW structure on the given closed four-manifold is stronger than finite-CW homotopy type. The 2025 monograph and later topology discussion retain the distinction; Borel-rigidity counterexamples do not answer it.

645.review_note: Current closing results cover contact-type, ellipsoid, near-periodic and other restricted Hamiltonian settings. They do not supply the specified compatible symplectic form and residual graph statement for every compact Euclidean hypersurface.

648.review_note: C1-density is known; higher-regularity results add center-bunching/coherence or center-dimension assumptions. The October expanding-on-average theorem is likewise restricted and does not prove general Cr-density for each r>=2.

649.review_note: The arbitrary-norm theorem is planar. Higher-dimensional Euclidean density integrality and fixed-integer-dimensional rectifiability in strictly convex Banach spaces do not prove integrality for all norms in dimension >=3.

650.review_note: The current October ALE revision assumes both toric and Hermitian structure. Almost-Kahler and prescribed-end/kernel cases also add hypotheses absent from the general simply connected Ricci-flat ALE question.

655.review_note: ICTV boundedness controls a more restricted auxiliary field, and first-order TV clipping arguments do not apply to unsmoothed second-order TGV. The 2026 spatial-parameter work still assumes bounded solutions where required; no theorem for every bounded datum and a,b>0 located.

659.review_note: The general periodic fully coupled three-dimensional SKT continuation question survives the 2026 local corrigendum. Triangular diffusion, equal base diffusivities, diagonal models or approximation conditional on a smooth reference impose extra assumptions.

661.review_note: The all-scales big-projection theorem is known and the planar single-scale branch is announced. Neither the planar theorem nor stronger projected-measure bounds settle the n>=2 single-scale projected-set lower-bound question.

663.review_note: The statistical existence theorem is not a polynomial-time algorithm. Direction-adaptive simultaneous accuracy with the spectral tail term is stronger than a Euclidean sub-Gaussian or a different Mahalanobis guarantee; no matching efficient construction located.

664.review_note: The d>=3 small-mixed-Holder question asks a Kolmogorov lower bound in the uniform target norm over every linear approximation space. Stronger Besov target norms, nonlinear sparse approximation and fixed-subspace errors do not supply it; no complete later result located.

045.review_note: The uniform constant for arbitrary scalar polynomials and arbitrary Hilbert-space dimension is still distinguished from Hartz's homogeneous-polynomial theorem. The July 2026 Szász paper also says norm equivalence is unknown; no later complete result found.

067.review_note: The July 2026 announcement settles only M=4 (eleven measurements). Generic sufficiency, almost-everywhere recovery and Gaussian-frame assertions do not determine the global existence minimum for all dimensions.

superseded_reviews.review_note: The 2026 general Faber–Krahn-position estimate retains log n. Unitarily invariant matrix balls and polytopes with O(n) facets are special cases, not the universal symmetric-body O(n) bound.
